title: Deploy a Third-Party PFX Certificate to Mobile Devices for App Use with Microsoft Intune
author_notes: Scenario/shaping note (internal): a third-party PFX (functioning like a software/license certificate an app consumes, not a standard TLS/SSL case) must reach iOS/mobile devices via Intune. The imported PFX object already exists in Intune/Graph for a service UPN, but the team could not complete delivery through the Intune UI/template path they were testing. Resolution must assess the CORRECT enterprise deployment method and how to assign/deploy for the app use case.

Key correction the solution must make: a static third-party PFX is NOT a SCEP/PKCS CA-issued scenario; the right paths are (a) a PKCS imported certificate configuration profile (needs the Intune Certificate Connector + a Graph PFX import) and/or (b) a custom iOS configuration profile carrying a PKCS12 payload. Choice is driven by how the APP accesses the identity in the keychain.
Effort tier: T3 (multi-component within Intune: imported-PFX vs custom-profile decision, Certificate Connector, Graph import, trusted-root chain, app keychain nuance, troubleshooting).
Do NOT print the customer's real tenant UPN/domain in deliverables — use a neutral placeholder (e.g. Intune.Cert.<service>@<your-domain>). version_directive: New; branding: off.
hook: Get a third-party PFX certificate onto iOS devices through Intune — the right way, so the app can actually use it
problem: A third-party PFX certificate — one that behaves like a software/license credential an app consumes, not a standard TLS/SSL cert — needs to land on iOS/mobile devices through Microsoft Intune so a specific app can use it. The usual trap: teams reach for the SCEP or PKCS (CA-issued) template, the request never shows up the way they expect, and the deployment stalls even though the PFX object already exists in Intune/Graph. The reason is simple once you see it: a static, externally-issued PFX is a different delivery path. This solution gives you the correct, repeatable enterprise method to import that PFX and deliver it to devices so the app can consume it.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — how certificate delivery works in Intune and why a static third-party PFX is NOT a SCEP/PKCS (CA-issued) scenario; the two correct paths — a PKCS imported certificate profile (with the Intune Certificate Connector + a Graph PFX import) and a custom iOS configuration profile carrying a PKCS12 payload — and a clear decision guide for the app use case (keychain access).

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Intune, Entra ID, the Intune Certificate Connector and its health, the third-party PFX file + password, the trusted root/intermediate chain, iOS enrollment, a pilot group) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide (the resolution) — exact, ordered steps: confirm the imported PFX object, install/validate the Certificate Connector, import the PFX via Microsoft Graph, deploy the trusted-root chain, create and assign the PKCS imported certificate profile (and the custom PKCS12 profile alternative), then validate the app can use the certificate, pilot, and expand.

App-use & keychain guidance — how the certificate is placed on iOS and what determines whether the target app can access the identity (keychain access group / app configuration), with the decision criteria for imported-PFX vs custom-profile delivery; app-internal specifics are deferred to the app vendor.

5 PowerShell scripts — certificate-readiness discovery (imported PFX objects + Connector + profiles), per-device certificate-presence validation, a fleet certificate-deployment report, safe remediation (re-assign/repair), and a Graph PFX-import helper that uploads a third-party PFX to Intune.
short: The correct, repeatable enterprise method to deliver a third-party PFX certificate to iOS/mobile devices via Intune for app use — imported-PFX (Certificate Connector + Graph import) vs custom PKCS12 profile, with a decision guide and the keychain nuance that determines whether the app can use it. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
short_plain: The correct enterprise method to deliver a third-party PFX certificate to iOS/mobile devices via Intune for app use — imported-PFX (Certificate Connector + Graph import) vs custom PKCS12 profile, with a decision guide and the keychain nuance.

bottom_line: A third-party PFX certificate correctly imported into Intune and delivered to iOS devices through the right profile type — with the app able to consume it — instead of stalling on the wrong SCEP/PKCS template, proven on a pilot before you scale.
